question.text: A ray of light through the point <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>A</mi><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><mn>1,2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></mfenced></math> strikes the plane <math><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>z</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>12</mn></math> at a point <math><mi>B</mi></math> and on reflection passes through the point <math><mi>C</mi><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><mn>3,5</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>9</mn></mrow></mfenced><mo>.</mo></math> If the equation of a plane containing the incident ray and the reflected ray is <math><mi>P</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math> and the distance of <math><mi>P</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math> from <math><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><mn>0,0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></mfenced></math> is <math><mi>λ</mi></math> units, then the value of <math><mn>13</mn><msup><mrow><mi>λ</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math> is equal to

solution.text:
A plane which contains the incident ray and the reflected ray must contain the points A,B,C and should be perpendicular to the given plane.
So, equation of the plane is x-1y-2z-3111236=0
⇒x-13-y-24+z-33-2=0
⇒3x-3-4y+8+z-3=0
⇒3x-4y+z+2=0
Hence, the distance of the plane from 0,0,0 is 0-0+0+29+16+1=226 units
